purposesTitle: What you can do on an e-Tourist visa
purposesIntro: The e-Tourist visa covers short, non-work visits to India.

purposes.title: Holidays and sightseeing
purposes.text: Touring India, beach breaks and city trips.

purposes.title: Short courses
purposes.text: Language, music, dance, arts, crafts or cooking courses of up to 6 months, without a qualifying certificate.

purposes.title: Short voluntary work
purposes.text: Unpaid volunteering for up to one month.

purposes.title: Mountaineering
purposes.text: Expeditions, with clearance from the Indian Mountaineering Foundation.

notCoveredTitle: Not covered by an e-Tourist visa
notCovered: Staying longer than the visa allows

documentsTable.details: A clear scan or photo of the page with your photo and details. Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months and have at least 2 blank pages.
Recent, in colour, front-facing with eyes open and no glasses. Plain white or light background, no shadows or borders. We crop and resize it for you.
Not required for the application, but useful to have when you travel.
For short courses or voluntary work: a letter from the organisation on its letterhead.
If you’re not a British citizen: your UK eVisa share code page, BRP or settlement document.

rules.title: How long you can stay
rules.text: On the 30-day visa you can stay 30 days from the day you first arrive. On the 1-year and 5-year visas you can stay up to 180 days in each calendar year.

rules.title: It can’t be extended or changed
rules.text: An e-Visa can’t be extended or switched to another type of visa once you’re in India, so choose the right one before you travel.

rules.title: Arrive at an approved airport or seaport
rules.text: You must enter India through one of the airports or seaports approved for e-Visas. All the main international airports are included, such as Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Goa and Kochi. You can leave from any immigration checkpoint.

rules.title: Who can’t use an e-Visa
rules.text: People of Pakistani origin, anyone with a military, police or security background (serving or retired), and holders of diplomatic or official passports must apply for a regular visa instead.

rules.title: Fill in the e-Arrival card
rules.text: Before you fly, complete India’s free e-Arrival card online within 72 hours of arrival. It’s arrival information, not a visa. [How the e-Arrival card works](/india-e-arrival-card/)

rules.title: No protected areas
rules.text: An e-Visa isn’t valid for protected, restricted or cantonment areas. Visiting places such as parts of the North East, Sikkim or the Andaman Islands may need a separate permit.

boxText: Pakistani origin, a military or police background, work, journalism or a longer stay all need a regular visa. We help with those too.

sections.heading: 30 days, 1 year or 5 years: which should I choose?
sections.text:
- [30-day e-Tourist visa](/india-30-day-e-tourist-visa/): best for a single holiday or one family visit. It lasts 30 days from the day you arrive.
- [1-year e-Tourist visa](/india-1-year-e-tourist-visa/): best if you might go back within the year. You can make many trips over 12 months.
- [5-year e-Tourist visa](/india-5-year-e-tourist-visa/): best if you visit family in India regularly. One application covers five years of trips.

The longer visas cost more, but often work out cheaper than applying again and again.

sections.heading: Indian tourist visa requirements for UK residents
sections.text:
You need a passport valid for at least 6 months from the date you apply, with two blank pages, a recent photo, and a scan of your passport photo page. You don’t need flight or hotel bookings to apply, but you must have a return or onward ticket and enough money for your stay when you travel.

The Indian e-Tourist visa is the same for British citizens and most other nationalities who can apply online.

sections.heading: How to apply for an Indian e-Tourist visa
sections.text:
Apply online at least 4 days before you arrive, and no more than 120 days before. With us, you answer simple questions, upload your passport and photo, and we fill in the official form, fix any photo problems and submit it. Your e-Visa is emailed to you once approved.

Most Indian e-Tourist visa applications are decided within a few working days.

faqs.q: Can I visit family on an e-Tourist visa?
faqs.a: Yes. Visiting family or friends is one of the main purposes of the e-Tourist visa.

faqs.q: Can I attend a wedding in India on an e-Tourist visa?
faqs.a: Yes. Going to a family wedding or celebration is a tourist visit.

faqs.q: How long can I stay on a 1-year or 5-year e-Tourist visa?
faqs.a: Up to 180 days in each calendar year, over as many trips as you like while the visa is valid.
At least 4 days before you arrive in India, and no more than 120 days before. We recommend applying 2 to 3 weeks ahead in case anything needs correcting.

faqs.q: Can I apply myself instead of using you?
faqs.a: Yes. You can apply on the official website, indianvisaonline.gov.in, and pay only the government fee. People use us when they want a person to check their eligibility, fix their photo and documents, and handle the form for them so nothing goes wrong.

faqs.q: What happens when I land in India?
faqs.a: Show your printed e-Visa (ETA) at immigration. Your fingerprints and photo are taken and the visa is stamped in your passport. You must arrive at an airport or seaport approved for e-Visas.
